svg.aria-label: Retrieval in PlaidCloud: a question drives tool selection by embedding similarity, keyword BM25 retrieval over the published documentation, and live permission-checked reads of your own data via analysis paths and MCP tools, producing a grounded answer.
svg.text: How Retrieval Works — Three Separate Lanes
Only the documentation lane is a retrieval index. Your business data is read live, on demand, under your permissions — it is never embedded into a vector store.
A question
"Why did the Operations
Results drop last quarter,
and how do I chart it?"
Asked from any surface
LANE 1 · WHICH TOOLS TO OFFER
Semantic tool selection
Tool descriptions — not your data — are embedded once and cached. The question is
matched against them so the model is offered only plausibly relevant tools.
A few tools are always present so the agent can orient itself.
If confidence is low, it falls back to the full tool list — a confident wrong pick is worse.
LANE 2 · HOW THE PRODUCT WORKS
Documentation retrieval (the actual RAG)
A keyword-ranking index (Okapi BM25) is built in memory over the published
documentation corpus — one entry per page, refreshed from the docs site.
The agent decides when to search, gets a ranked shortlist, then fetches one page
or a single section of it — so irrelevant pages never enter the context window.
Public product documentation only. No customer content is in this index.
LANE 3 · WHAT YOUR DATA SAYS
Live, permission-checked reads — not retrieval
Analysis paths resolve a friendly name — "the Operations Results", "the P&L" — to a
real project and table, so nobody has to restate where the data lives.
The agent then reads schema, rows, dimension members, and allocation lineage
through MCP tools, one checked call at a time, at the moment it is asked.
Answers reflect the data as it is right now, not as it was when something was indexed.
A grounded answer
Real query results, with
the documentation page
cited when it was used.
Carries a confidence signal
and plain-language caveats.
Says "I don't know" rather
than inventing a number.
Grounding is not training. Nothing retrieved here is used to train a model, and the retrieval index holds published documentation — never your tables.
